Phase D documents are the slice immediately after the middle band, because the middle band itself was replayed in Phase R and would be double-warmed
band replay order is newest->middle->oldest so the (expected) evicted band's re-insertion cannot perturb the resident bands measured before it

beyond the card's minimum protocol the unit spent 8 declared boundary-probe requests (6 search + 2 confirmation, cap 16) because the three replay bands bracket the eviction onset only to 128 documents while the card requires the onset point; every probe is a byte-identical re-send of a pooled document (no new content, no reconfiguration)

the resident capacity W is inferred from hit/miss recency-rank inequalities under the stated model 'one document evicted per inserted document, oldest-touched first'; the model is self-checking (a contradiction would surface as W_lo > W_hi, which did not occur) and an independent submission-position formulation gives the same bracket

token-pool LRU (188 documents at 1.62M tokens) is excluded by the observation that the middle band at 1.18-1.26M cumulative tokens (0.73-0.78x capacity) is fully evicted; the 30-31 document cap is reported as measured, not as a configuration name
